text: Code 0 is not applicable for this chapter.
The cortex of a bone is the dense outer shell that provides strength to the bone; the spongy center of a bone is the cancellous portion.
The periosteum of the bone is the fibrous membrane covering of a bone that contains the blood vessels and nerves; the periosteum is similar to the capsule on a visceral organ.

For the spinal tumors (C412), if only the number of adjacent vertebral segments below are involved, this would be localized (code 1). Any other vertebral segments involved (non-adjacent) would be regional (code 2).

The four pelvic segments used in these codes are:
Acetabulum
Iliac wing
Pubic ramus/Symphysis/Ischium
Sacrum
Regional lymph nodes are defined as those in the vicinity of the primary tumor.
If there is no mention of lymph node involvement clinically, assume that lymph nodes are negative.
